## Summary

Every Formal AI draft that Hive Mind ran on its own repository since 2026-10-04 began with this message:

> Let me open e.g and read what it says.

It then called `read` on `<workspace>/e.g` and got `Error: File not found: /tmp/gh-issue-solver-1791368974521/e.g`. This happened in 10 of 10 runs that reached the model (formal-ai 0.352.1, temperature 0), so it is deterministic. The other run, 37367087072, was cancelled and kept no log.

- Runs: [37204604042](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/actions/runs/37204604042), [37237191915](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/actions/runs/37237191915), [37338018685](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/actions/runs/37338018685), [37442158538](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/actions/runs/37442158538), [37488162642](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/actions/runs/37488162642), [37530569498](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/actions/runs/37530569498), [37533446090](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/actions/runs/37533446090), [37585287501](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/actions/runs/37585287501), [37603515653](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/actions/runs/37603515653), [37606848542](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/actions/runs/37606848542), [37628867214](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/actions/runs/37628867214).
- Full job log with the stream: [job-112744304123-formal-ai-draft.log](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2625-ba46c90ff692/dev/log/issues/2625/pulls/2626/ci-logs/job-112744304123-formal-ai-draft.log), lines 2533 and 2644–2737.
- Found while investigating link-assistant/hive-mind#2625.

## Root cause

Hive Mind's prompt contains the ordinary English abbreviation `(e.g., …` several times, for example "When WebFetch tool fails to retrieve expected content (e.g., returns empty content, …)".

In `rust/src/agentic_coding/file_read.rs` (main, d209aac):

1. `local_file_paths` splits on whitespace and passes `(e.g.,` to `clean_file_token`.
2. `peel_sentence_punctuation` strips `(` and `,`. `trim_trailing_sentence_dot` then strips the final `.`, which leaves `e.g`.
3. `looks_like_local_file_path("e.g")` accepts the token: the stem is `e`, the extension is `g` (1 to 12 characters), and every character is a path character.
4. The prompt contains a read cue, so `file_read_task_for` returns `FileReadTask::Direct { path: "e.g" }`. The planner then narrates `response_agentic_action_read_en` and emits `read`.

`i.e.` and `a.k.a.` take the same path. `etc.` and `vs.` do not, because they have no inner dot.

## Reproduction

This is a line-for-line JS port of the tokenizer: [experiments/formal-ai-eg-path-token-2625.mjs](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2625-ba46c90ff692/experiments/formal-ai-eg-path-token-2625.mjs)

```
$ node experiments/formal-ai-eg-path-token-2625.mjs
tokens taken as local files: [ 'e.g', 'README.md', 'i.e' ]
  "(e.g.,"   → "e.g"    file-like: true
  "e.g."     → "e.g"    file-like: true
  "(i.e."    → "i.e"    file-like: true
  "etc."     → "etc"    file-like: false
  "vs."      → "vs"     file-like: false
  "a.k.a."   → "a.k.a"  file-like: true
```

A Rust regression test for `file_read.rs`:

```rust
#[test]
fn latin_abbreviations_are_not_local_files() {
    let prompt = "When WebFetch fails to retrieve content (e.g., returns empty content), read README.md (i.e. the docs).";
    assert_eq!(local_file_paths(prompt), vec!["README.md".to_owned()]);
    for token in ["e.g", "i.e", "a.k.a", "E.g"] {
        assert!(!looks_like_local_file_path(token), "{token}");
    }
}
```

## Workaround

Write "for example" or "that is" in prompts sent to Formal AI. A client cannot do this reliably, though, because issue bodies and user text contain the abbreviations too.

## Suggested fix

In `looks_like_local_file_path`, for a token without `/`, reject dotted abbreviations: tokens where every dot-separated segment is one or two letters (`e.g`, `i.e`, `a.k.a`, `n.b`). For example:

```rust
fn is_dotted_abbreviation(token: &str) -> bool {
    token.contains('.') && token.split('.').all(|s| (1..=2).contains(&s.len()) && s.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphabetic()))
}
```

Call it next to `is_dotted_number`. A stricter alternative is to accept a bare (slash-less) token only when its extension is a known file extension, as `solver_handlers/web_search_intent.rs::probable_local_file_name` already does. Either change would also cover the write-request parser and the shell route that share `file_path_shape`.

comments.body:
Independently reproduced with the installed formal-ai **0.352.1** binary while investigating [hive-mind #2613](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/2613), which lost two real draft sessions to `File not found: .../e.g`.

The bounded local `/v1/chat/completions` replay uses temperature 0 and a `read(filePath)` tool:

```text
Read README.md (e.g., the project documentation).
  → read("README.md"), read("e.g")

Read README.md, for example the project documentation.
  → read("README.md")
```

The control supports replacing this abbreviation with “for example” as a limited prompt workaround. It does not make arbitrary issue text safe to rewrite.

The [reusable replay](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2613-2efa14ce78a7/experiments/issue-2613/replay-formal-ai.mjs) limits requests, memory, stack, CPU time and wall time. [Complete responses](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2613-2efa14ce78a7/docs/case-studies/issue-2613/evidence/formal-ai-replay.json) and the [real workflow failure](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2613-2efa14ce78a7/docs/case-studies/issue-2613/evidence/formal-job-2613.log#L4268) are preserved in the case study.

An additional observation: after returning a tool response for **each** requested call, including `Error: File not found: e.g` for the invalid path, the minimal recipe formats that error as the contents of `e.g`. The real Agent integration instead ends with the file-not-found error. Successful API startup therefore does not establish that the issue was solved.

The shared path predicate fix proposed here should include abbreviation cases (`e.g`, `i.e`, `a.k.a`) alongside real filenames and tests where a read cue occurs elsewhere in the prompt. A separate regression should keep tool failures recognizable as errors rather than successful file contents.

title: Agentic read routes the abbreviation "e.g." to a file read: every Hive Mind draft starts with "Let me open e.g"
